title: Migrate async metrics to OpenTelemetry collector and remove sync side-effects from queue workers
creator: Miguel Torres
description: Problem: our hot-path async workers (Redis and Kafka consumers) still use a mix of synchronous metrics sinks and blocking side-effects. We observed periodic p95/p99 latency spikes caused by synchronous metric increments, buffered writes to Prometheus pushgateway, and legacy logging that forces thread context switches. This ticket will migrate the async worker metrics to OpenTelemetry (OTel) with a local collector, switch to non-blocking counters/histograms, and remove leftover synchronous calls in the delivery/retry paths. The goal is to reduce tail latency and make metric emission safe in the hot loop.
background: Recent incident (2026-01-03) showed worker p99 token latency rising during bursts; root-cause analysis pointed to blocking pushgateway flushes and synchronous redis client calls in the metrics path. We also discovered high-cardinality labels created by per-tenant debug tags being emitted indiscriminately. Prior tickets touched similar areas (ENG-708331 upgrade-redis-client), but we still have residues and metric-side blocking.
tasks: Audit all metric calls in consumer and retry codepaths and catalog synchronous sinks
Add non-blocking OTel counters/histograms wrappers for hot-path usage
Introduce a local sidecar OTel Collector configuration (batch processor + resource limits)
Replace Pushgateway/statsd usages in workers with OTel exporter over UDP or OTLP gRPC depending on env
Upgrade redis client on the consumer runtime to async-native API and remove blocking shims
Remove per-message synchronous debug-label emission and add sampling rules for high-cardinality labels
Add integration tests validating non-blocking behavior under load
Run load benchmarks before/after and record p50/p95/p99 and throughput
Rollout plan: feature flag + canary on 10% tenants -> 50% -> 100% with monitoring dashboards
Document migration steps for Dedicated and Private deployments (collector config and env toggles)
acceptance_criteria: No synchronous metric sinks called from the hot-path (delivery/retry loops) in runtime codebase
End-to-end benchmark shows >=25% reduction in p99 latency under synthetic burst profile or absolute p99 < 80ms for the benchmark harness
Production canary shows no increase in error rate and stable CPU/memory profile for workers
OTel collector config checked into infra repo and included in Private deployment docs
A migration playbook with rollback steps and feature-flag toggles exists and is reviewed by SRE
risks: Collector misconfiguration can drop metrics if batch window is too large—monitor acceptable latency for observability
OTLP gRPC adds CPU overhead; must profile collector resource needs to avoid new resource pressure
Changing labels (sampling) will affect dashboards and historical alerting—coordinate with monitoring owners
Redis client upgrade may reveal subtle concurrency issues—keep backout plan to previous client version
